name: Moby
context: Guest. Richard Melville Hall - DJ, singer, songwriter and producer, author of two memoirs and subject of the documentary Moby Doc. He got his start DJing in the basement at Mars, broke out with Go, and talks about being sober, shy and Christian in the late-80s club scene

name: Michael Alig
context: Moby says he and Michael were weirdly close at the turn of the 90s and that he loved him: as Moby saw him then, Michael was gentle, joyful and the architect of a celebratory scene, before the drugs took over. Michael introduced the new DJ to Peter Gatien at the Limelight. Michael later pleaded guilty to manslaughter for the killing of Angel Melendez

name: New York
context: Moby finally worked up the courage to move there; nightlife was a refuge from a city torn apart by violence, he says

name: Mars (nightclub)
context: Rudolf Piper's club where Moby got his first big gig: he dropped off a demo tape and a DJ resume with the woman hiring busboys, she laughed, and Yuki called him back. He played the basement and then the first floor; Chip Duckett ran a Sunday gay night there. As James tells it, Michael says he worked on the club's look until Rudolf fired him two weeks before it opened and announced there would be no club kids

name: Peter Gatien
context: Moby recalls Michael taking him into Peter's office when he was a new Limelight DJ; Peter looked at him, said nothing and went back to work, and Moby wondered if he was fired. James was talking to Peter recently: he remembered asking whether this Moby was worth $300

name: Danceteria
context: Where Fenton and Randy DJ'd, and where Moby, at a Mission of Burma and Bad Brains show in 1983, walked upstairs into the hip-hop room and the gay dance room - his first taste of celebratory dance culture

name: James St. James
context: Host; tells Moby that Porcelain, the song, is the closest he will get to time travel

name: Randy Barbato
context: Co-host; he and Fenton skipped editing class at film school for happy hour at the Pyramid

name: DJ Keoki
context: Moby knew him well at the turn of the 90s and was briefly in a band with him. Years later, at a date of Perry Farrell's ENIT festival, Moby asked how he and Michael were; as Moby tells it, Keoki looked ashen and said things were not good. James says he still DJs and they have been in touch since Michael died

name: Fenton Bailey
context: Co-host; says he and Randy were hopeless DJs who just played the Studio 54 album at Danceteria

name: Moby's abandoned-factory squat
context: Moby says he lived in a vast abandoned factory in Connecticut, paying security guards to squat, with a gay porn production company on one side, no running water and a little electric heater. $100 was about 5% of his yearly income. James pictures the loft in Diva

name: Go (Moby song)
context: Moby's first big hit: released as a minimal techno track that sold a thousand copies, then remixed with Twin Peaks in it into a top-ten single in Europe, South America and Asia. For a while he was introduced as 'Moby Go'

name: Then It Fell Apart (Moby memoir)
heard: then it all fell apart / the second memoir
context: Moby's second memoir. He says the first book did okay but the second sold little, yet plenty of people who hadn't read it had strong opinions about it; a Christmas Day party in it still makes readers angry

name: Limelight
context: Where Moby DJ'd for $100 a night and met Peter Gatien; Michael's L train outlaw party ended there, and Evergreen played its one show there

name: Porcelain (Moby memoir)
context: Moby's first memoir, covering his New York years from the late 80s through the 90s - the abandoned factory, Mars and the record shops. James calls it beautifully written; Moby says his agent told him that if he claims Herman Melville as an ancestor he has to write his own book, and he found he loved writing and editing

name: Los Angeles
context: Where Fenton first met Moby, and where all four now live - 'the first city of the apocalypse', Moby jokes

name: Pyramid Club
context: Fenton and Randy's first taste of drag - skipping class for happy hour; White Horse and Book of Love's Boy were Pyramid records; Moby first met Chip Duckett there

name: Yuki (Mars investor)
context: Booked the DJs at Mars: Moby's tape somehow reached him and he left a message on Moby's answering machine - still the most exciting moment of Moby's working life

name: Madonna
context: Mark Kamins discovered her at Danceteria; at Moby's second-ever live show, at Le Palace de Beauté, she looked him up and down and said he was very talented, as James tells it

name: Connecticut
context: Moby lived in an abandoned factory in a rough part of the state, without running water, and took the train into New York

name: Michael's L train outlaw party
heard: an outlaw party on the L train
context: One of Moby's favourite memories: he and his friend Lee walked into the L train stop at 14th and Third and the train pulled in with a thousand people screaming; Michael had it stop at Sixth Avenue so everyone walked up to the Limelight

name: Rudolf Piper
context: Owner of Mars; Moby later played at Quick, which James calls Rudolf's place

name: Frankie Knuckles
context: Moby first met him at Dance Tracks and couldn't believe he was in the same room; at the record-store counter the royalty, like Frankie, stood at the front

name: NASA raves (Shelter)
context: James: where New York's rave scene peaked, in the old Area space, with Scotto on lights, Gabriel on the door and DJ Soulslinger. Moby found it a more suburban, more conservative crowd, and there called out a British rave band for a homophobic remark

name: Chi Chi Valenti & Johnny Dynell
context: Moby's celebrity-DJ hero lived across the street from him with Chi Chi; he couldn't believe he was talking to them - the royalty of royalty. They still look fantastic, Moby says, and should be on the show

name: Moby Doc
context: The new documentary about Moby: nonlinear, with animated bits, reenactments by friends and conversations with David Lynch and David Bowie. Moby apologises for the pun and says he never reads reviews

name: The vegan, Christian, straight-edge, bald DJ
heard: the vegan, Christian, straight-edge, bald DJ
context: How people described Moby in the late-80s club scene, James says - sober, shy and DJing at sex parties

name: Chloë Sevigny
context: James says she always tells him how intimidated she was by the club kids, when they were the ones in awe of her - the same thing he says about Moby

name: Chip Duckett
context: Ran a phenomenal Sunday gay night at Mars; he did nights at the Pyramid forever, Moby says

name: Michael's white-powder guessing game
context: As James tells it, at the Limelight Michael would line up rails of different white powders and whoever guessed which was which got to do them all

name: Moby's Danceteria epiphany
context: After the punk bands, Moby walked upstairs at Danceteria into the hip-hop DJ and then the gay DJ's room - his Saul-on-the-road-to-Damascus moment. In LA, the land of fiction, he decides Fenton and Randy were the DJs, so he owes them both

name: Traci Lords
context: DJing on the ENIT bill; James calls her a spectacular, wise woman

name: Steve Lewis
context: Put together the band Evergreen with Moby, Keoki and his wife Jennifer

name: Julie Jewels
context: Moby was friends with her, James says

name: Michael's club-kid dinner
context: Moby walked in, saw Waltpaper and Jenny Talia, decided everyone was much cooler than him and was struck mute by shyness; James remembers everyone being in awe of Moby

name: Waltpaper
context: At Michael's dinner where Moby felt everyone was cooler than him; also a guest Fenton praises

name: Diva (1981 film)
context: James imagines Moby's factory like the giant loft in the French opera thriller, with a bathtub in the middle and a girlfriend roller-skating around; Fenton points out Diva was glossy and the factory was not

name: The factory loft and Diva's bathtub
heard: a bathtub in the middle of the loft ... roller skates
context: James's fantasy of Moby's squat: the Diva loft, a bathtub in the middle and a girl roller-skating around - Moby's reality was a space heater and no running water

name: Lee (Moby's friend)
context: Rode his motorcycle through the factory and went with Moby to the L train party

name: Congo Bill's
context: The room at Danceteria where Fenton and Randy threw parties and DJ'd, with Michael the busboy asking for Heart of Glass

name: 14th Street
context: Moby's apartment at 14th and Third, by the L train; Johnny Dynell and Chi Chi Valenti lived across the street

name: Interview magazine
context: Moby's girlfriend worked there and told him Mars was hiring; his ex Janet, also at Interview, introduced him to Michael Musto

name: Willi Ninja
context: James says you knew you'd made it when he turned up on your dance floor - he did at Moby's first night on the Mars first floor

name: Voguing
context: In 1989 voguing was at its peak: houses came down to the middle of the Mars first floor for ad-hoc competitions, Moby remembers

name: Friday record-store scrum
heard: every Friday night ... a record store
context: On Friday afternoons the new records came in: DJs crushed against the counter, the royalty - Frankie Knuckles, Junior Vasquez, Red Alert, Clark Kent - at the front, and when one of them nodded at a record, everybody wanted it

name: Hells Angels
context: Moby says his mum dated Hells Angels and other oddballs; Dance Tracks was right by their clubhouse

name: Laid Back – 'White Horse'
heard: if you wanna ride, ride the White Horse
context: For Fenton, the Pyramid's record

name: Book of Love – 'Boy'
context: Very much a Pyramid track, Fenton says

name: Dominatrix – 'The Dominatrix Sleeps Tonight'
context: Randy can't place the name; James had it play at his 19th birthday party - the coolest thing that had happened to him

name: Lower Manhattan
context: Where those club hits were inescapable - and outside it no one had heard of them

name: Miami
context: Moby's first Miami show: the flyer billed 'Mob 9 singing their hit' - every single thing wrong, he says

name: Area
context: The space NASA took over, James says, and one of the names of the club on Hubert Street

name: Quick (club)
context: Rudolf's place in the club building on Hubert Street, which Moby also lists as Shelter and Area; Moby played there

name: United Kingdom
context: Moby flew there for Top of the Pops; a British rave band was the one he called out at NASA

name: Hugging on ecstasy, stacked on ketamine
heard: hugging each other and holding hands ... stacked in corners
context: The 90s dance floor: on ecstasy everyone hugged and held hands; once ketamine took over they sat, stacked in corners on top of each other

name: DJ Soulslinger
context: The NASA DJ

name: Herman Melville
context: Moby's agent: if you claim Melville as a descendant you have to at least try to write the book yourself

name: Dianne Brill
context: Fenton says she has a tremendous amount to say on the show; Moby saw her across a nightclub and felt, like in Spinal Tap, he wasn't even allowed to look at her

name: Michael Musto
context: Moby felt he was meeting New York royalty in the flesh when his ex-girlfriend Janet introduced them; one of the show's guests Fenton praises

name: Bad Brains
context: The other band that night

name: Stephen Saban
context: One of Moby's heroes from back then - meeting him felt like meeting the biggest movie star on the planet; in the days after a party you'd check whether he'd written about you, James says

name: Maripol
context: Moby played his second-ever live solo show with Maripol's husband; about 30 people came, two of them O.J. Simpson and Madonna, he says

name: Moby's show for Madonna and O.J.
context: Moby's early live show: they promoted it hard, about 30 people came, and two of them were O.J. Simpson and Madonna. James: that's New York nightlife - 30 people in a room and one of them is Madonna

name: O.J. Simpson
context: In the small crowd at Moby's early live show, as Moby tells it

name: 'Porcelain' – Moby
context: James: the closest he will ever get to time travel - it takes him straight back to a specific room, a specific boy and a specific K-hole

name: Perry Farrell
context: Started the ENIT festival after Lollapalooza and rounded up electronic acts like Keoki, Moby and Traci Lords

name: Keoki ENIT meeting
context: Moby asks Keoki, DJing on the same ENIT festival bill, how things are and how Michael is; as Moby tells it, Keoki looks ashen and says things are not good, in a way that invites no more questions

name: 'Tomorrow Never Knows' – The Beatles
heard: Tomorrow Never Dies by The Beatles
context: Evergreen's one cover at the Limelight

name: Gawker
context: In its early days Moby read everything about himself there, comments and all

name: Gothamist
context: Ditto - until one hateful comment made him stop reading about himself

name: World of Wonder (WOW)
context: Fenton and Randy are its co-founders

name: The middle-aged bald club
context: Moby recognises the hosts from 'our middle-aged guy bald club'; James protests he is still a twunk

name: Granny at the rave
heard: granny at the rave / gray wigs / a walker
context: At 25 James was already called granny at the raves - so he turned up with a walker and grey wigs as a joke

name: Project X
context: James first really knew of Moby through an interview he did with the club kids' magazine

name: Jenny Dembrow aka Jenny Talia
context: Also at that dinner

name: Clara the Carefree Chicken
context: Moby says he would have met James around the time he met Clara the Chicken

name: A Night at Studio 54
context: Fenton admits that as DJs they just put on the Studio 54 pre-mixed album and played the whole thing

name: 'Heart of Glass' – Blondie
context: Michael the busboy's standing request, Fenton says

name: McDonald's
context: Michael took Fenton and Randy there for dinner to learn how to throw parties

name: Sixth Avenue
context: Where Michael stopped the L train party so everyone walked up to the Limelight

name: Lady Bunny
context: Moby met her around the time he met Chip Duckett, maybe at Wigstock

name: Wigstock
context: Back when it was still in Tompkins Square Park or on the piers

name: Tompkins Square Park
context: Early Wigstock

name: Mark Kamins
context: Supposed to play at Mars the night Moby was hired last minute for the first floor; Moby notes he discovered Madonna at Danceteria

name: Voguing houses on the Mars first floor
heard: these houses coming down to have ad-hoc competitions
context: In 1989, as Moby remembers it, houses came down to the middle of the floor for ad-hoc vogue battles and Willi Ninja was on the dance floor

name: Canal Street
context: James's first guess for where the DJs went for new records on Fridays

name: Vinyl Mania
context: The big DJ record shop on Carmine Street

name: Carmine Street
context: Home of Vinyl Mania

name: Times Square
context: Where Moby remembers a record shop called Disco-Rama or Disco Mania

name: Dance Tracks
context: The East Village record shop by the Hells Angels where Moby first met Frankie Knuckles

name: East Village
context: Dance Tracks' neighbourhood

name: 4th Street
context: Where Moby places Dance Tracks in the East Village, right by the Hells Angels

name: Junior Vasquez
context: Record-store royalty, at the front of the Friday counter

name: DJ Red Alert
context: Hip-hop DJ royalty at the record-store counter

name: DJ Clark Kent
context: Another hip-hop DJ the shops brought to the front

name: DJ Dmitry
context: Dmitry from Deee-Lite: a nod from him at the counter and everyone wanted the record

name: Deee-Lite
context: Dmitry's band

name: Raze – 'Break 4 Love'
context: One of the records Moby would put his hand up for at the counter

name: Doug Lazy – 'Let It Roll'
context: Another must-have from the counter

name: 'Sweet Pussy Pauline'
context: James's example of a club hit that never travelled far beyond New York

name: Strafe – 'Set It Off'
context: A nine-minute New York smash that cleared floors outside the city: Moby played it in the suburbs and people walked off

name: Twin Peaks
context: Moby's remix of Go that included elements of Twin Peaks became the hit

name: Europe
context: Go was a top-ten single there

name: Top of the Pops
context: Moby flew from his abandoned factory to the UK to do the show between Michael Jackson and Phil Collins

name: Michael Jackson
context: On Top of the Pops on either side of Moby, with Phil Collins

name: Phil Collins
context: The other one

name: Larry Levan
context: One of the legend DJs of the 70s and 80s

name: John 'Jellybean' Benitez
context: Another of the legends

name: Seth Green
context: Moby still thinks of Seth Green playing James, making ketamine on a baking tray in the kitchen - with a giant rat

name: Party Monster (2003)
context: The film with the ketamine-on-a-baking-tray scene and the talking rat

name: The Tunnel
context: James starts to say Tunnel, then corrects himself to the Limelight

name: Gabriel (NASA door)
context: Did the door at NASA, James says

name: Scotto
context: Did the lights at NASA

name: Fashion Institute of Technology
context: 80s New York was people who went to FIT or Parsons paying $80 a month rent

name: Parsons School of Design
context: Same

name: New Jersey
context: Where much of the NASA crowd came in from

name: Long Island
context: Same

name: Upstate New York
context: Same

name: Ernie Glam
context: One of the show's guests Fenton praises as brilliant

name: Lake Hollywood
context: Moby wrote much of Porcelain in the pool house of his first LA house, drinking organic white tea and looking out at Lake Hollywood

name: Mission of Burma
context: One of the bands Moby went to Danceteria to see the night of his epiphany

name: Anita Sarko
context: James remembers her on Danceteria's ground floor playing Scraping Foetus off the Wheel as if to clear the dance floor; Moby felt in the presence of royalty when he finally met her

name: Scraping Foetus off the Wheel
context: What Anita Sarko would play to drive people off the dance floor, James says

name: Paper magazine
context: The other place he read about them

name: The Village Voice
context: Where Moby always saw names like Anita Sarko's

name: This Is Spinal Tap
context: How Moby felt seeing Dianne Brill across a club - as if he wasn't allowed to look at her

name: Janet (Moby's ex-girlfriend)
context: Worked at Interview and became friends with Michael Musto

name: Beauregard Houston-Montgomery
context: Moby met him with Michael Musto: New York royalty in the flesh

name: Wayne's World
context: Meeting Michael Musto and Beauregard felt like that scene in Wayne's World

name: La Palace de Beauté
context: Where James places Moby's early live show with Maripol, the night Madonna came; the name was also Larry Tee's dance act, with RuPaul and Lahoma dancing

name: Madonna looks Moby up and down
context: At his early live show Madonna looked Moby up and down, said 'you're very talented' and walked away, as James tells it

name: Monica Lewinsky
context: James compares Traci Lords to her: both came out the other side wise

name: Disappearance of Angel Melendez
context: James wonders whether Keoki's 'not good' came at the time Angel went missing

name: Lollapalooza
context: Moby had done it before Perry Farrell's ENIT tour

name: ENIT Festival
context: Perry Farrell's travelling festival after Lollapalooza, with electronic dance acts on the bill; where Moby saw Keoki again

name: Evergreen (Steve Lewis's band)
context: The band Steve Lewis put together with Moby on keyboards, Keoki DJing and Steve's wife Jennifer singing; it lasted about a day and played one show at the Limelight - a cover of the Beatles' Tomorrow Never Knows. James doesn't remember it, and he remembers everything

name: John Lennon
context: Moby corrects himself: Evergreen's cover was the Beatles' - John Lennon's - Tomorrow Never Knows

name: Death of Michael Alig
context: Since then, James says, they have all been in more contact with Keoki

name: Susanne Bartsch
context: 'The woman who threw the New Year's Eve ball' - nightlife royalty in Moby's eyes

name: Moby-Dick
context: James was 20 minutes into Moby Doc before he got the pun

context: In conversation with Moby in Moby Doc

name: David Bowie
context: Also in Moby Doc

context: 'Never read the comments' - the first rule of Drag Race, Moby says

context: Shaved head, thick black-framed glasses, a grey goatee and neck tattoos, in a plain black T-shirt, in a white home studio with square acoustic panels, a black electric guitar, a rack of gear, a red shell chair and headphones on the daybed

name: James's on-camera look (S01E09)
context: Bald, black rectangular glasses, a black jacket over a white shirt with a wide open collar, in front of his floor-to-ceiling bookshelves with a white studio microphone in the corner

name: Fenton's on-camera look (S01E09)
context: Clear-framed glasses and a royal-blue T-shirt with red stripes, in front of floor-length grey-green curtains with a white microphone at his side
